## Today's Agenda

Two-Factor (Two-Way) Analysis of Variance

- The importance of interaction
- Interpreting ANOVA output
- What are the key model checks for ANOVA?
- Comparing Model Performance Indices
- What if we add a covariate?

```{r}

#| message: false
```

## Favorite Movies Data

```{r}

```

## Describing Today's Variables {.smaller}

- Favorite movies from students in 2020-2026

 Variable | Description |
---------------:|:-------------------------------------------------------
`mov_id` | M-xxx code to identify movie
`metascore` | **outcome**: critic rating (0 to 100) pulled from [Metacritic](https://www.metacritic.com/)
`drama` | Is drama one of the [IMDB](https://www.imdb.com/) genres for this movie? (1 = yes, 0 = no)
`comedy` | Is comedy one of the [IMDB](https://www.imdb.com/) genres for this movie? (1 = yes, 0 = no)
`bacon_s1` | Bacon number (from [Oracle of Bacon](https://oracleofbacon.org/)) for movie's first listed star
`rt_audience` | Audience rating (0 to 100) from [Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/)
`movie` | Movie Name to identify movie

- Bacon number = # of movies it takes to connect the star to Kevin Bacon. 
  - Bacon = 1: star has been in a movie with Kevin Bacon.
  - None of our 282 movies feature Kevin Bacon, as it turns out.

## Today's analytic data

```{r}
#| echo: true
mov_18 <- mov_raw |>
  select(mov_id, metascore, drama, comedy, bacon_s1, rt_audience, movie) |>
  mutate(drama = factor(drama), comedy = factor(comedy),
         bacon_s1 = factor(bacon_s1), movie = as.character(movie))

mov_18 |> gt_preview(top_n = 5, bottom_n = 1, incl_rownums = TRUE) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = 24)
```

## Dealing with missing values

```{r}
#| echo: true

miss_var_summary(mov_18) |> filter(n_miss > 0) |> 
  gt() |> tab_options(table.font.size = 20)
miss_case_table(mov_18) |> 
  gt() |> tab_options(table.font.size = 20)
```

## Can we assume MCAR?

Can we use data to assess whether assuming **MCAR** is reasonable?

```{r}
#| echo: true

mov_18 |> mcar_test()
```

With a high chi-square statistic and tiny *p* value from the [Little (1988) test](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01621459.1988.10478722), we conclude that there is essentially no evidence that the data are missing completely at random.

- So we should be highly motivated to impute.

## Today's Imputation Strategy

Today, we'll assume **MAR** and impute all missing values, including `metascore`, which will be our outcome. 

- Another approach we'll often use would be to impute everything **except for** the outcome.

How many imputations should we consider running?

```{r}
#| echo: true
mov_18 |> pct_miss_case()
```

### Building 10 imputations

```{r}
#| echo: true
set.seed(20261027)

mov_18_mice10 <- mice(mov_18, m = 10, printFlag = FALSE)
```

## Two Primary Analytic Data Sets

```{r}
#| echo: true

## complete cases
mov_cc <- mov_18 |> drop_na()
dim(mov_cc)
n_miss(mov_cc)
```

### Selecting a single imputation

```{r}
#| echo: true
## arbitrarily chose to look at the third imputation of 10
mov_i3 <- complete(mov_18_mice10, 3) |> tibble()

dim(mov_i3)
n_miss(mov_i3)
```

## Example 1

Suppose we want to simultaneously understand the impacts of two factors on `metascore`, specifically:

- `drama` (1 or 0)
- `comedy` (1 or 0), and

and it is possible that the impact of `comedy` on `metascore` may depend on whether the movie is also a `drama` (i.e. `comedy` and `drama` may **interact**.)

- For a start, we'll analyze the data with **complete cases**.

## Looking at our two factors

```{r}
#| echo: true
mov_cc |> count(drama, comedy) |> 
  gt() |> tab_options(table.font.size = 24) |>
  opt_stylize(style = 6, color = "blue", add_row_striping = TRUE)
```

## An interaction plot is a plot of means.

Calculate and store the group means.

```{r}
#| echo: true
ex1_means <- mov_cc |>
  group_by(comedy, drama) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean_metascore = mean(metascore))

ex1_means
```

## How strong is the interaction?

Now, we'll plot these means, and look for a substantial interaction (non-parallel lines.)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

ggplot(ex1_means, aes(x = drama, y = mean_metascore)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = comedy, color = comedy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = comedy)) +
  scale_color_material() +
  labs(title = "Example 1 Interaction Plot",
       subtitle = "Do we see substantially non-parallel lines?",
       y = "Metascore (0-100)", 
       x = "Drama (1 = yes, 0 = no)", 
       color = "Comedy",
       caption = "Complete Cases (n = 264 movies)")
```

## Two-Way ANOVA without interaction

This model predicts our outcome (`metascore`) using the two factors as main effects only (with no interaction.)

```{r}
#| echo: true

mainfx <- lm(metascore ~ drama + comedy, data = mov_cc)

mainfx
```

$$
metascore = 71.024 + 3.501 (drama = 1) - 5.709 (comedy = 1) 
$$

## Interpret the drama estimate: 3.50?

```{r}
#| echo: true
model_parameters(mainfx, ci = 0.90, pretty_names = FALSE)
```

If we have two movies with the same `comedy` status, but only one has a `drama` = 1, then **on average** the dramatic movie will have a metascore that is 3.50 points higher than the movie which is not a drama, according to our `mainfx` model.

## Interpret the estimate: -5.71?

```{r}
#| echo: true
model_parameters(mainfx, ci = 0.90, pretty_names = FALSE)
```

Our `mainfx` model estimates that if we have two movies with the same drama status, but one is a comedy and the other is not, then **on average** the comedy will have a metascore that is 5.71 points lower than the movie which is not a comedy.

## Interpret the intercept term?

```{r}
#| echo: true
model_parameters(mainfx, ci = 0.90, pretty_names = FALSE)
```

71.02 is the intercept. It's the `mainfx` model's estimate of the mean of `metascore` across all movies where both `drama` is 0 and `comedy` is 0.

## ANOVA table for `mainfx`

```{r}
#| echo: true
anova(mainfx)
```

### % of Total SS explained by the two factors?

-   Total SS = 1340 + 1976 + 63484 = 66800
-   So % explained = (1340 + 1976) / 66800 = 0.0496, or 4.96%

## Model `mainfx` and its assumptions

- `mainfx` is a "main effects only" model. It assumes there is zero interaction between `drama` and `comedy` in predicting `metascore`.
- Like any ANOVA model, `mainfx` makes the usual linear model assumptions (linearity, constant variance, Normality)
    - Focus: posterior predictive check, and Normal Q-Q plot of residuals[^1].

[^1]: The assessment of linearity and non-constant variance used by `check_model()` are best used when we have at least one quantitative predictor in our model.

## Checking model `mainfx`

```{r}
#| echo: true
set.seed(20264311)
check_model(mainfx, check = c("pp_check", "qq"), detrend = FALSE)
```

## Interaction Plot, again

```{r}
#| echo: false

ggplot(ex1_means, aes(x = drama, y = mean_metascore)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = comedy, color = comedy)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = comedy)) +
  scale_color_material() +
  labs(title = "Example 1 Interaction Plot",
       subtitle = "Do we see substantially non-parallel lines?",
       y = "Metascore (0-100)", 
       x = "Drama (1 = yes, 0 = no)", 
       color = "Comedy")
```

## Two-Way ANOVA with Interaction

Fit the linear model, including an interaction (`*`) between our factors.

```{r}
#| echo: true

withint <- lm(metascore ~ drama * comedy, data = mov_cc)

withint
```

## `withint` model equation?

$$
metascore = 70.544 + 4.245 (drama = 1) - 4.740 (comedy = 1) \\
- 1.814 (drama = 1) \times (comedy = 1)
$$

`drama` | `comedy` | Estimated `metascore`
:---------: | :--------: | -------------:
0 | 0 | 70.544  
0 | 1 | 70.544 - 4.740 = 65.804
1 | 0 | 70.544 + 4.245 = 74.789
1 | 1 | 70.544 + 4.245 - 4.740 - 1.814 = 68.235

## Effect of `comedy` = 1?

Est. `metascore` | `comedy` = 0 | `comedy` = 1
:---------: | :--------: | :----------:
`drama` = 0 | 70.544 | 65.804  
`drama` = 1 | 74.789 | 68.235

- If `drama` = 0, difference between `comedy` = 0 and `comedy` = 1 estimates is 4.740 (70.544 - 65.804)
- If `drama` = 1, difference between `comedy` = 0 and `comedy` = 1 estimates is 6.554 (74.789 - 68.235)
- So the model's estimated effect of `comedy` **depends** on `drama`.

## Effect of `drama` = 1?

Est. `metascore` | `comedy` = 0 | `comedy` = 1
:---------: | :--------: | :----------:
`drama` = 0 | 70.544 | 65.804  
`drama` = 1 | 74.789 | 68.235

- If `comedy` = 0, difference between `drama` = 1 and `drama` = 0 estimates is 4.245 (74.789 - 70.544)
- If `comedy` = 1, difference between `drama` = 1 and `drama` = 0 estimates is 2.431 (68.235 - 65.804)
- So the model's estimated effect of `drama` **depends** on `comedy`.

## ANOVA table for `withint` model

```{r}
#| echo: true
anova(withint)
```

- Total SS = 1340 + 1976 + 50 + 63435 = 66801
- % explained = (1340 + 1976 + 50) / 66801 = 0.0504, or 5.04%
- Is this a big improvement over the `mainfx` model?

## Checking model `withint`

```{r}
#| echo: true
set.seed(20264312)
check_model(withint, check = c("pp_check", "qq"), detrend = FALSE)
```

## Compare performance of our two models?

```{r}
#| echo: true

compare_performance(mainfx, withint, rank = TRUE)
```

## Plot to compare performance indicators

```{r}
#| echo: true
plot(compare_performance(mainfx, withint))
```

## Do we have a substantial interaction?

- Interaction plot shows essentially parallel lines.
- % of variation explained by the interaction term is less than 0.1% of the variation in `meta_score`, overall.
- p value for the interaction term is pretty large ($p$ = 0.65)
- Is there a substantial improvement in the fit with the interaction?
    - Only in terms of raw $R^2$ and RMSE.

## What if we used the single imputation instead?

**In this example, nothing important changes** as it turns out.

- We'll largely skip through the slides from here to the standing break, but you can review them on your own to see that nothing substantial has changed as a result of including a few more movies.
- Doesn't mean that nothing *could have* changed, but not much did, in this case.

## Example 2

For the rest of today's work, we'll use the singly imputed data.

Suppose that we now want to understand the impact on `metascore`, of:

- `drama` (1 or 0), and
- `bacon_s1` (1, 2 or 3)

and it's possible that the impact of drama on metascore may depend on the first-listed star's Bacon number, and vice versa.

## Build an interaction plot

Calculate and store group means.

```{r}
#| echo: true
ex2_means <- mov_i3 |>
  group_by(drama, bacon_s1) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean_metascore = mean(metascore))

ex2_means
```

## How strong is the interaction?

Now, we'll plot these means, and look for a substantial interaction (non-parallel lines.)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

ggplot(ex2_means, aes(x = bacon_s1, y = mean_metascore)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = drama, color = drama)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = drama)) +
  scale_color_material() +
  labs(title = "Example 2 Interaction Plot",
       subtitle = "Do we see substantially non-parallel lines?",
       y = "Metascore (mean)", 
       x = "Bacon score for Star 1", 
       color = "Drama?",
       caption = "Single Imputation: n = 282 movies")
```

## Example 2: Two-Way ANOVA models 

```{r}
#| echo: true

mainfx2 <- lm(metascore ~ bacon_s1 + drama, data = mov_i3)
withint2 <- lm(metascore ~ bacon_s1 * drama, data = mov_i3)

compare_performance(mainfx2, withint2, rank = TRUE)
```

## Plotting Performance Indices

```{r}
#| echo: true

plot(compare_performance(mainfx2, withint2))
```

## Interpret `mainfx2` estimates?

```{r}
#| echo: true
model_parameters(mainfx2, ci = 0.90, pretty_names = FALSE)
```

$$
metascore = 65.39 + 2.98 (Bacon = 2) + 8.15 (Bacon = 3) \\
+ 4.35 (drama = 1) 
$$

## Making Predictions with `mainfx2`

```{r}
#| echo: true
estimate_relation(mainfx2, ci = 0.90)
```

## Specify `withint2` equation?

```{r}
#| echo: true
model_parameters(withint2, ci = 0.90, pretty_names = FALSE)
```

## Making Predictions with `withint2`

```{r}
#| echo: true
estimate_relation(withint2, ci = 0.90)
```

## ANOVA for `mainfx2` model

```{r}
#| echo: true
anova(mainfx2)
```

## % of Total SS explained by the two factors?

```{r}
#| echo: true

eta_squared(anova(mainfx2))
```

## ANOVA table for interaction model

```{r}
#| echo: true
anova(withint2)
```

## % of Total SS explained by the factors?

```{r}
#| echo: true

eta_squared(anova(withint2))
```

## Checking model `mainfx2`

```{r}
#| echo: true
set.seed(20264315)
check_model(mainfx2, check = c("pp_check", "qq"), detrend = FALSE)
```

## Checking model `withint2`

```{r}
#| echo: true
set.seed(20264316)
check_model(withint2, check = c("pp_check", "qq"), detrend = FALSE)
```

## Substantial interaction here?

- Interaction plot shows substantially non-parallel lines.
- Interaction term explains about 1% of the variation in `metascore`, overall.
- p value for the interaction term: ($p$ = 0.13)
- Substantial improvement in the fit with interaction?
    - 5/7 in-sample performance indices prefer interaction

What do you think?

## Treating Bacon number as quantitative?

We make a lot of little decisions. Are our conclusions robust?

```{r}
#| echo: true

mov_i3_extra <- mov_i3 |> mutate(bacon = as.numeric(bacon_s1))

anova(lm(metascore ~ drama * bacon, data = mov_i3_extra))
```

## Example 3

What if we add `rt_audience` as a covariate?

- We might consider centering `rt_audience`. 
- Here is an **analysis of covariance** model.

```{r}
#| echo: true
fit3 <- lm(metascore ~ drama * bacon_s1 + center(rt_audience), 
           data = mov_i3)
```

## Our ANCOVA model `fit3`

```{r}
#| echo: true

anova(fit3)
```

## Variation explained by this model?

```{r}
#| echo: true

eta_squared(fit3)
```

## Drop Interaction Term?

```{r}
#| echo: true
fit3_noint <- lm(metascore ~ drama + bacon_s1 + center(rt_audience),
             data = mov_i3)

anova(fit3_noint)
```

## Compare three models?

```{r}
#| echo: true

compare_performance(withint2, fit3, fit3_noint, rank = TRUE)
```

## Compare performance plot?

```{r}
#| echo: true

plot(compare_performance(withint2, fit3, fit3_noint))
```

## Check model `fit3` (1/3)

```{r}
#| echo: true
check_model(fit3, check = c("pp_check", "qq"), detrend = FALSE)
```

## Check model `fit3` (2/3)

```{r}
#| echo: true
check_model(fit3, check = c("linearity", "homogeneity"))
```

## Check model `fit3` (3/3)

```{r}
#| echo: true
check_model(fit3, check = c("outliers", "vif"))
```
